commands.title: Collect a Windows technician baseline
commands.summary: Capture OS, device, uptime, memory, volume, disk and network details.
commands.code:
Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object CsName,WindowsProductName,WindowsVersion,OsBuildNumber,OsArchitecture,CsManufacturer,CsModel
Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object LastBootUpTime,TotalVisibleMemorySize,FreePhysicalMemory
Get-Volume | Select-Object DriveLetter,FileSystem,HealthStatus,SizeRemaining,Size
Get-PhysicalDisk | Format-Table FriendlyName,MediaType,HealthStatus,OperationalStatus,Size -AutoSize
Get-NetIPConfiguration
commands.safety: Read-only inventory. Output may expose customer hostnames, serials, usernames and IP addresses. Sanitize before sharing outside the private service record.

commands.title: Open the built-in Windows diagnostic consoles
commands.summary: Open Resource Monitor, Reliability Monitor, System Information, Event Viewer and DirectX diagnostics.
commands.code:
Start-Process resmon
Start-Process perfmon.exe -ArgumentList '/rel'
Start-Process msinfo32.exe
Start-Process eventvwr.msc
Start-Process dxdiag.exe
commands.safety: Opens local diagnostic utilities; no repair is performed. Logs and reports can contain identifying system information.

commands.title: Find processes using the most CPU and memory
commands.summary: Capture current top CPU and working-set consumers and open Resource Monitor.
commands.safety: A point-in-time snapshot, not proof of a leak. Repeat while the user reproduces the slowdown; do not terminate processes solely from this ranking.

commands.title: Inspect recent crashes and unexpected shutdowns
commands.summary: Read recent Kernel-Power, unexpected-shutdown and bugcheck events.
commands.safety: Read-only. Event IDs are symptoms and timeline evidence, not a root-cause diagnosis. Sanitize host and path details before sharing.

commands.title: Inventory disks before cloning or recovery
commands.summary: Identify disks by model, serial, capacity, bus type and health before selecting a source or target.
commands.safety: Read-only inventory. Physically verify disk identity before imaging or formatting. For a failing source, avoid stress tests and write repairs; follow image-first recovery.

commands.title: Diagnose IP, DNS and HTTPS reachability
commands.summary: Separate adapter configuration, DNS resolution and TCP connectivity checks.
commands.code:
Get-NetIPConfiguration
Resolve-DnsName learn.microsoft.com
Test-NetConnection learn.microsoft.com -Port 443 -InformationLevel Detailed
commands.safety: Read-only network tests. Replace the example host with an approved endpoint when testing internal services. A successful public test does not prove internal DNS or VPN health.

commands.title: Repair Windows component store and system files
commands.summary: Run supported DISM component-store repair followed by System File Checker.
commands.safety: State-changing repair. Use a stable power connection and an appropriate repair source if DISM requests one. Run DISM first, let it finish, then SFC. Review exit results and logs; reboot only when indicated.

commands.title: Check component-store health without repairing
commands.summary: Inspect Windows component-store health before choosing a repair path.
commands.safety: Diagnostic scan. It may take time but does not apply the RestoreHealth repair. Run on a stable machine and retain relevant logs.

commands.title: Extract recent SFC repair findings
commands.summary: Inspect System File Checker entries from the CBS log.
commands.safety: Read-only log extraction. CBS entries may include paths and machine context; keep raw logs private and redact before external sharing.

commands.title: Scan an NTFS volume for file-system errors
commands.summary: Run an online scan of the C: volume without requesting an offline repair.
commands.safety: Online scan, not a substitute for imaging a failing disk. If SMART or hardware symptoms indicate imminent failure, stop and image first. Do not add /f or /r without a recovery plan and backup.

commands.title: Inspect Microsoft Defender protection and signatures
commands.summary: Check antivirus, real-time protection and signature freshness.
commands.safety: Read-only. Defender cmdlets and fields vary by Windows edition and security-provider ownership. A healthy status is not proof that a device is uncompromised.

commands.title: Update Microsoft Defender security intelligence
commands.summary: Request the latest Defender security intelligence updates.
commands.safety: Changes security intelligence on the endpoint and requires Defender to be available. Confirm the endpoint's active security product and management policy first; verify signature time afterward.

commands.title: Start a Microsoft Defender full scan
commands.summary: Run a full scan after confirming Defender is the active primary antivirus product.
commands.safety: Starts a potentially long scan. This does not replace incident containment or offline analysis. Record scope, completion and detections; third-party AV ownership can limit Defender cmdlets.

commands.title: List WinGet application updates
commands.summary: Preview applications WinGet can identify for update.
commands.safety: Inventory only. Review package identity, publisher, version, source and pins before choosing updates. Some apps are not managed by WinGet.

commands.title: Update all identified WinGet applications
commands.summary: Apply available WinGet updates with interactive installers where supported.
commands.safety: Changes installed software. Preview with `winget upgrade` first, check business app compatibility, close affected apps, confirm maintenance window and retain installer prompts. Some packages may require separate vendor update mechanisms.

commands.title: Include packages with unknown installed versions
commands.summary: Update WinGet packages even when WinGet cannot determine their installed version.
commands.safety: Higher uncertainty than a normal upgrade-all run. Preview first, review each candidate and avoid using this as a blind unattended fleet update. Pinned packages remain governed by their pin policy.

commands.title: Check Chocolatey installation and outdated packages
commands.summary: Check whether Chocolatey is installed and list packages with updates.
commands.code:
Get-Command choco -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (Get-Command choco -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { choco outdated }
commands.safety: Read-only package inventory. Package visibility depends on configured sources, licenses, pins and Chocolatey edition.

commands.title: Preview a Chocolatey upgrade-all operation
commands.summary: Use Chocolatey's no-operation mode to inspect the upgrade-all plan.
commands.safety: No-op preview. Review package IDs, sources, pins and package scripts. Chocolatey package install scripts are code and can make system-wide changes during an actual upgrade.

commands.title: Upgrade all Chocolatey-managed packages
commands.summary: Apply Chocolatey package updates after reviewing the no-op preview.
commands.safety: State-changing operation. Run `choco outdated` and `choco upgrade all --noop` first. Review sources, package scripts, exclusions and pins; use a maintenance window and keep recovery options. Do not add --force or --ignore-pinned by default.

commands.title: Check Scoop package updates
commands.summary: Show Scoop-managed apps and their available update status.
commands.safety: Read-only package inventory. Scoop manages only packages installed through its buckets; it does not cover all Windows applications.

commands.title: Update Scoop apps
commands.summary: Refresh Scoop manifests and update Scoop-managed applications.
commands.safety: Changes user-installed software. Preview with `scoop status`, check app compatibility and use a backup/rollback route for important developer tools.

commands.title: Open Windows Update settings
commands.summary: Open the supported Windows Update interface for OS servicing.
commands.safety: Opens Settings only. Review update policy, safeguard holds, active hours and reboot requirements. Do not bypass organizational update management.

commands.title: Open Microsoft Store app updates
commands.summary: Open the Store downloads and updates page.
commands.safety: Opens the Store UI. Review pending updates and managed-device policy before applying.

commands.title: Install Chocolatey CLI through WinGet
commands.summary: Install Chocolatey using its documented WinGet package ID rather than executing a downloaded bootstrap script.
commands.code:
winget show --id chocolatey.chocolatey --exact --source winget
winget install --id chocolatey.chocolatey --exact --source winget --interactive
commands.safety: Installs a machine-level package manager. Verify publisher, package ID, source and organization policy first. Chocolatey packages can run installer scripts; inspect package metadata and sources before use.

commands.title: Install Microsoft Sysinternals Suite
commands.summary: Install Microsoft's Sysinternals Suite through WinGet after checking its package identity.
commands.code:
winget show --id Microsoft.SysinternalsSuite --exact --source winget
winget install --id Microsoft.SysinternalsSuite --exact --source winget --interactive
commands.safety: Installs a suite of powerful diagnostic utilities. Verify the Microsoft publisher and package metadata; Sysinternals tools can inspect process, file, registry and network activity.

commands.title: Install Microsoft PowerToys
commands.summary: Install Microsoft's utility collection through WinGet.
commands.code:
winget show --id Microsoft.PowerToys --exact --source winget
winget install --id Microsoft.PowerToys --exact --source winget --interactive
commands.safety: Installs software after package details are displayed. Check architecture, scope and managed-device policy first.

commands.title: Download Chris Titus Tech WinUtil for inspection
commands.summary: Download the upstream WinUtil launcher to a review folder instead of piping remote code directly into the current PowerShell process.
commands.code:
$review = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Downloads\INTA-Toolkit-Review'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $review -Force | Out-Null
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://christitus.com/win' -OutFile (Join-Path $review 'winutil.ps1')
Get-FileHash (Join-Path $review 'winutil.ps1') -Algorithm SHA256
notepad (Join-Path $review 'winutil.ps1')
commands.safety: Downloads but does not execute the script. Review the entire script and upstream repository/release before running. WinUtil requires Administrator for system-wide changes and includes tweak/update controls; inspect each selected change and its undo path.

commands.title: Launch a reviewed local WinUtil script
commands.summary: Run the local WinUtil script only after inspecting it and confirming the upstream source.
commands.code:
$script = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Downloads\INTA-Toolkit-Review\winutil.ps1'
if (-not (Test-Path $script)) { throw 'Download and inspect WinUtil first.' }
Get-FileHash $script -Algorithm SHA256
notepad $script
# After inspection, run explicitly:
& $script
commands.safety: Runs a third-party administrator utility that can install apps, change Windows settings, apply tweaks and manage updates. Confirm current upstream source, read selected actions, create a recovery point where appropriate, and never blindly apply debloat/privacy presets to customer or managed devices.

commands.title: Open the official Tron Script distribution instructions
commands.summary: Open the Tron Script maintainer's distribution instructions; do not download the GitHub source repository as if it were the full runnable package.
commands.safety: Tron is a long-running, invasive multi-stage repair/cleanup script. The maintainer explicitly warns that GitHub source alone is not the runnable package. Review current instructions, verify the release's SHA-256/PGP integrity, read stage actions and logs, preserve data, and use only with explicit customer authorization. It can take hours and changes/deletes system state.

commands.title: List Debian/Ubuntu package updates
commands.summary: Refresh package metadata and list upgradable packages.
commands.safety: Refreshes package metadata and displays candidates; does not install package upgrades. Confirm repositories and held packages.

commands.title: Upgrade Debian/Ubuntu packages
commands.summary: Apply available package upgrades after reviewing the package list.
commands.code:
sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade
commands.safety: Changes installed packages. Review removals and dependency changes before confirming; avoid `full-upgrade` on production systems without a planned change and recovery route.

commands.title: Check Fedora/RHEL package updates
commands.summary: Check available updates without applying them.
commands.safety: Returns update availability; exit code 100 can indicate updates are available and is not necessarily an error.

commands.title: Upgrade Fedora/RHEL packages
commands.summary: Apply package updates after reviewing repository and package changes.
commands.safety: Changes installed packages. Review transaction summary, kernel changes and service restart/reboot requirements before confirming.

commands.title: Check Arch Linux package updates
commands.summary: Refresh package database and inspect pending updates using the package manager's supported query path.
commands.safety: Requires the checkupdates helper from pacman-contrib on many systems. Do not partially upgrade Arch systems; read the news and follow full-upgrade guidance.

commands.title: Perform a full Arch Linux upgrade
commands.summary: Synchronize repositories and perform the supported full system upgrade.
commands.safety: Changes the entire installed system. Arch does not support partial upgrades; read Arch news first and avoid interrupting package transactions.

workflows.title: Windows first-response diagnostics
workflows.description: Build a compact evidence baseline before making changes.
workflows.sequence: Run the baseline, open the relevant diagnostic console, then collect only the evidence related to the symptom.
workflows.warning: Sanitize diagnostic output before sharing it.

workflows.title: Windows component repair
workflows.description: Inspect component health, repair Windows and verify protected files.
workflows.sequence: Run the read-only health checks first. Run DISM RestoreHealth only when appropriate, then SFC. Review the CBS log if SFC reports unresolved corruption.
workflows.warning: Requires administrator privileges and can change Windows servicing state.

workflows.title: Defender security check
workflows.description: Check protection, update signatures and launch a full scan when Defender is the active provider.
workflows.sequence: Check the active AV provider first. Update signatures, then run a full scan if justified. For active incidents, follow the ransomware/incident playbook.
workflows.warning: A scan is not a substitute for containment, forensic preservation or a clean rebuild when compromise is confirmed.

workflows.title: Windows application maintenance
workflows.description: Inventory WinGet, Chocolatey and Scoop updates before applying a controlled update batch.
workflows.sequence: Preview each manager separately. Confirm package IDs, publishers, pinned/excluded packages, app compatibility and maintenance window. Apply only the manager(s) actually used on this device.
workflows.warning: Do not assume one package manager sees every installed application. Do not blindly combine managers or bypass pins.

workflows.title: Install a technician essentials kit
workflows.description: Install trusted diagnostic utilities after checking package metadata.
workflows.sequence: Check each exact package ID and publisher. Install only the tools needed for this job. Keep portable utilities in the INTA Toolbox where licensing and publisher distribution permit.
workflows.warning: Installing software changes the endpoint. HWiNFO, commercial utilities and third-party tools may have technician-use licensing restrictions.

workflows.title: Cross-platform package maintenance
workflows.description: Use the correct full-upgrade workflow for the Linux distribution.
workflows.sequence: Identify the distribution first. Run only its matching package-manager commands. Do not mix package managers or partially upgrade Arch Linux.
workflows.warning: Package upgrades can restart services or require a reboot. Use an approved maintenance window.

toolkits.name: Microsoft Sysinternals Suite
toolkits.summary: Process Explorer, Process Monitor, Autoruns, RAMMap, TCPView and more for deep Windows diagnosis.
toolkits.trust: Microsoft publisher; verify the package source and signature.

toolkits.name: Chris Titus Tech WinUtil
toolkits.summary: All-in-one app installation, tweaks, fixes, configuration and Windows update management. Powerful; review every selected change.
toolkits.trust: Community-maintained PowerShell utility. Administrator required for system-wide changes; do not blindly apply presets.

toolkits.name: Tron Script
toolkits.summary: Multi-stage PC cleanup, disinfection, repair and patch workflow. Long-running and invasive; use only after reading current stage documentation.
toolkits.trust: Maintainer says GitHub source is not the complete runnable package. Obtain the full package through the maintainer's distribution instructions and verify integrity.

toolkits.name: Chocolatey CLI
toolkits.summary: Package manager with package inventory, no-op previews, install and upgrade operations.
toolkits.trust: Review package source, package scripts, pins and license/edition.

toolkits.name: Windows Package Manager (WinGet)
toolkits.summary: Microsoft package manager for searching, inspecting, installing and updating Windows apps.
toolkits.trust: Prefer exact package IDs and source/publisher verification.

toolkits.name: Scoop
toolkits.summary: User-oriented command-line package manager, useful for developer and portable app workflows.
toolkits.trust: Review bucket source and manifest scripts; do not add unknown buckets blindly.

toolkits.name: UniGetUI
toolkits.summary: Graphical package-manager front end for supported package managers; useful when a technician wants a visual review of package updates.
toolkits.trust: Use its official release page and verify the publisher; package coverage depends on configured managers.
